channel.title: Use & Like: app news
channel.description: What changed in the apps you use, in our own words, with what it means for you and what to do about it.

item.title: iPhone storage full before the holidays: iCloud vs Google Photos
item.description: When your iPhone storage is full of photos, iCloud Photos with Optimize iPhone Storage and Google Photos' Free up space can both move the full-size pictures to the cloud, but each counts against a free limit, 5 GB at Apple and 15 GB at Google, and deleting works differently in each.

item.title: Monitor refresh rate stuck at 60Hz: how to check it on Windows and Mac
item.description: A monitor sold as 120Hz or 144Hz only runs that fast when the computer is set to it, and the Refresh Rate setting in Windows or macOS shows what yours uses; if the higher number is missing, the cable, the port or the driver is often the limit.

item.title: New Apple Health app explained: Insights, Longevity and Health Age
item.description: The new Apple Health app comes with iOS 27.3, which 9to5Mac expects in December: it adds an Insights tab with daily summaries, a Longevity tab with a Health Age score and at-home movement checks, but only on an iPhone 15 Pro or newer with Apple Intelligence turned on.

item.title: Claude install as app: turn Artifacts into Mac and Windows desktop apps
item.description: Claude can now install an Artifact you built in chat as its own app on a Mac or Windows PC, with an icon and window that open outside Claude. It's a beta for all plans, including free accounts.

item.title: Android Auto black screen: Google Maps not loading for some drivers
item.description: Some Android Auto users report that Google Maps doesn't load when Android Auto starts, so the car's screen shows black where the map should be. Most reports come from Ford owners, and Google hasn't commented yet.

item.title: Apple Watch voice recorder app Tapkeep turns your day into text
item.description: Tapkeep records your day from an Apple Watch with one tap, then turns the audio into text on your iPhone, split into titled conversations you can search. It costs $9.99 once with no subscription, and was #86 among paid Lifestyle apps on the US App Store on 24 November.

item.title: AreaMap: land area measure app for iPhone shows acres and lot lines
item.description: AreaMap measures a piece of land when you tap its corners on a satellite map or walk its edge with GPS, and shows county lot lines. The free iPhone and iPad app was #36 in Utilities on the US App Store on 24 November.

item.title: Buy now pay later on Black Friday: fees, interest and credit scores
item.description: Buy now pay later splits a purchase into payments: pay-in-4 plans from PayPal, Afterpay and Affirm charge no interest, monthly plans can cost up to about 36% a year, and whether a plan shows up on your credit report depends on the company.

item.title: CBeebies shows on Netflix from 2 December in a new hub
item.description: The BBC is putting 24 CBeebies preschool shows, including Hey Duggee, Numberblocks and Teletubbies, in their own hub on Netflix from 2 December in the UK, Ireland, the US, Canada and Australia, as a six-month trial.

item.title: ChatGPT flight search: Dohop's WAYA plugin finds bookable flights
item.description: Travel company Dohop added its WAYA flight search to ChatGPT: you pick a direct or multi-airline trip in the chat, then book it on the airline's own checkout page, where you can add seats and bags.

item.title: Duo Remote: remote desktop iPhone app for Windows PCs and Macs
item.description: Duo Remote is a new $1.99 iPhone app that shows and controls your Windows PC over Remote Desktop or your Mac over its built-in Screen Sharing. It was #99 in paid Productivity apps on the US App Store on 24 November.

item.title: Encrypted RCS messaging between iPhone and Android explained
item.description: Texts between iPhones and Android phones can be end-to-end encrypted since Apple and Google started rolling it out in beta on 11 May 2026, but only over RCS, with iOS 26.5 or later, the latest Google Messages and a supported carrier.

item.title: First Light: sunrise alarm app for iPhone using your HomeKit lights
item.description: First Light fades your dimmable HomeKit lights up from red to daylight each morning, so you wake without an alarm sound. It costs 3.99 dollars once and was #87 among paid Lifestyle apps on the US App Store on 24 November.

item.title: Galaxy S27 Ultra camera downgrade leak: no laser autofocus or 3x zoom
item.description: Leaker Ice Universe says Samsung will remove the laser autofocus from the Galaxy S27 Ultra, and he and OnLeaks both expect the 3x telephoto camera to go, leaving three rear cameras. Samsung hasn't confirmed either.

item.title: iOS 27 Notification Center swipe changed: it now opens from the top-left
item.description: On iPhones and iPads with Siri AI turned on, a swipe down from the middle of the top edge now opens Siri, and Notification Center opens from the top-left corner instead. Without Siri AI, the swipe works as before.

item.title: iPhone Handoff on iOS 27: which carriers support it and what it costs
item.description: iOS 27's iPhone Handoff, which moves your number between two iPhones, works on T-Mobile ($5 a month), EE (£5) and Telekom in Germany (€6.95). Verizon says it will add it for $10 a month with no date, and AT&T has no plans.

item.title: Kagi Mail: new Gmail alternative with no ads opens public beta
item.description: Kagi, the company behind a paid search engine and the Orion browser, opened a public beta of Kagi Mail, an email and calendar service with no ads and no user profiling. It costs 99 dollars a year after a 60-day free trial and comes at no extra cost with Kagi Ultimate.

item.title: NIVA free design tool: a browser studio with no templates or AI
item.description: British artist Stuart Semple has launched NIVA, a free design tool that runs in the browser and puts photo editing, vector drawing and page layout in one place. It has no subscription, no templates and no AI that makes the design for you.

item.title: PDA Notes app brings the Newton notepad back on iPhone and iPad
item.description: PDA Notes from Enfour recreates the notepad of Apple's 1990s Newton pen computer, drawn pixel for pixel, for iPhone and iPad. Out since 19 November for 19.99 dollars, it was #47 among paid Productivity apps on the US App Store on 24 November.

item.title: Pixel November update not showing on T-Mobile, Mint and Tello
item.description: Two weeks after Google released the November Pixel Drop on 10 November, many Pixel phones on T-Mobile and the Mint and Tello networks are still on the October update, though a few owners now report it installing.

item.title: Pocket Paintbox: watercolor and oil painting app for iPhone and iPad
item.description: Pocket Paintbox is a new painting app for iPhone and iPad with watercolor, gouache, oil and ink that you mix in little paint wells like a real paintbox. It costs $4.99 once, with no in-app purchases listed, and was #26 among paid Graphics & Design apps on the US App Store on 24 November.

item.title: Ruke Knit knitting pattern app: follow patterns step by step on iPhone
item.description: Ruke Knit, out since 24 November for iPhone and iPad, lets you pick a knitting pattern and size, then follow the instructions in the app and check off each step as you go. It costs $9.99, and a $9.99 monthly subscription opens all its subscription patterns.

item.title: Spar Black Friday giveaway on Facebook is a phishing scam
item.description: A link going around Facebook in South Africa promises a free "MySpar Black Friday Sale" prize, but it leads to a phishing site that collects personal details. Spar says it isn't its promotion.

item.title: Spotify logged me out: outage hit logins on 24 November, now fixed
item.description: A Spotify outage on 24 November signed people out on phones and computers and showed a false "incorrect username and password" error, so many thought their account had been hacked. Spotify says the problem is fixed and asks anyone still signed out to log in again.

item.title: Spotify Running Mode now in India and 10 more countries
item.description: Spotify Premium subscribers in India, Germany, the Netherlands, the Philippines, South Africa, Nigeria and five more countries can now use Running Mode, which builds a soundtrack that matches the beat to your running pace.

item.title: Threads iPad app is out, and cashtags show live stock prices
item.description: Meta's Threads now has its own app for the iPad's big screen, released in an overnight update on 24 November. Threads is also adding cashtags: a $ sign and a stock ticker that open a page with live prices and charts.

item.title: Tidal AI music ban: fully AI-generated tracks removed from 9 December
item.description: Tidal will reject and remove tracks made entirely with AI from 9 December; songs where artists only used AI tools along the way stay. Until now Tidal tagged fully AI tracks and paid them no royalties.

item.title: TikTok down on 24 November: feed, search and profiles stopped loading
item.description: TikTok was down for many users on Tuesday afternoon, US time: For You videos, search results, favorites and profile pages didn't load in the iPhone and Android apps or on the web. It worked again by about 3:45 p.m. Eastern time.

item.title: Uber robotaxi with Lucid starts driverless tests in the Bay Area
item.description: Uber, Lucid and Nuro began testing their robotaxis with no one at the wheel in Palo Alto, Mountain View, Los Altos and Sunnyvale. Public rides through the Uber app are planned for early 2027.

item.title: Use old router as access point: how it works and what you lose
item.description: An old router can add Wi-Fi to a weak room as an access point, connected to your main router by cable, while the main router keeps running the network; set up as a second full router, it can break gaming, port forwarding and printer sharing.

item.title: VOSKI: offline translator app for iPhone for two people, one phone
item.description: VOSKI is a new 99-cent offline translator app for two people talking on one iPhone or iPad: each person speaks in turn and the app reads the translation aloud. It was #64 in paid Travel apps on the US App Store on 24 November.

item.title: WalkAware: Apple Watch app shows nearby places and landmarks
item.description: WalkAware lists museums, libraries, historic buildings and other landmarks near you right on your Apple Watch, using Apple Maps and Wikidata. It costs $2.99 with no subscription, account or ads, and was #63 among paid Travel apps on the US App Store on 24 November.

item.title: Walmart Apple Pay removed from the app and website weeks after adding it
item.description: Walmart no longer offers Apple Pay at checkout in its iPhone app or on its website, only weeks after it added the option. Apple Pay still works at Walmart's US stores.

item.title: WhatsApp dual camera mode in testing: film with front and back camera
item.description: WhatsApp is testing a camera mode on Android that records with the front and back camera at the same time, WABetaInfo reports. It's reaching some beta testers with version 2.26.46.9; WhatsApp hasn't said when everyone gets it.

item.title: Willow dictation keyboard on iPhone: dictate without switching apps
item.description: Willow's iPhone keyboard now lets you dictate right inside the app you're typing in, instead of jumping to Willow and back. Version 2.0 for iOS, launched on Product Hunt on 24 November, also adds swipe typing, smarter autocorrect, emoji and cursor control.

item.title: Windows 11 RAM usage: Microsoft's own apps now use 860 MB less
item.description: Microsoft said at Ignite 2026 that its own apps on Windows 11 now use over 860 MB less memory: Office 360 MB less, and Defender, Purview and OneDrive together over half a gigabyte less.

item.title: Wins Garden: daily wins journal app grows a flower for each day
item.description: Wins Garden is a journal app for writing down what you got done each day, big or small, and each day you log becomes a flower in a garden. It costs $1.99 and was #85 among paid Lifestyle apps on the US App Store on 24 November.

item.title: Xfinity price increase December 2026: what's known so far
item.description: Comcast says some Xfinity prices go up starting in December 2026 but hasn't published the amounts. Its Broadcast TV Fee for local ABC, CBS, FOX and NBC stations is already over 42 dollars a month in some areas.

item.title: Yebbi: free ink painting app for iPhone with brushes that react to touch
item.description: Yebbi is a free ink painting studio for iPhone with four brushes, Round, Dry, Soft Wash and Ink Splash, that respond to how you press, move and lift your finger. It was #92 among free Graphics & Design apps on the US App Store on 24 November.

item.title: WhatsApp Web: India warns to log out on shared computers
item.description: India's Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) says WhatsApp Web sessions left open on office, cyber café or other shared computers are being used to take over accounts and commit fraud. Closing the browser window doesn't end the session, so the advisory asks users to log out by hand every time.

item.title: 10 new photo and video apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These camera and editing apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Photo & Video charts this week, from film-look cameras and a VHS camcorder to a teleprompter and a RAW editor.

item.title: 10 new productivity apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These productivity apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Productivity charts this week, from a handwriting notebook and a talking keyboard to planners, countdowns and a shift calendar.

item.title: 10 new travel apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These travel apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Travel charts this week, from a gas price finder and Connecticut's mobile ID to translators, cruise port guides and a plane radar.

item.title: 10 new weather apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These weather apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Weather charts this week, from 3D storm radar and hurricane prep to northern lights odds and snow forecasts.

item.title: 5 new lifestyle apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These lifestyle apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's paid Lifestyle chart this week, from a pocket typewriter for letters to a Christmas countdown and a private journal.

item.title: 7 new music apps for iPhone climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These music apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Music charts this week, from record and cassette players for your Apple Music library to a free drum machine and a four-track recorder.

item.title: 7 new utility apps for iPhone climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These utility apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Utilities charts this week, from widgets and a keyboard for the foldable iPhone Duo to Google Wallet's new iPhone app.

item.title: 9 new health and fitness apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These health and fitness apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's paid Health & Fitness charts this week, from a step graph for the Apple Watch and a running app to a newborn log and breathing exercises.

item.title: Apple Wallet Connecticut driver's license and ID coming in 2027
item.description: Connecticut residents will be able to add a driver's license or state ID to Apple Wallet on iPhone and Apple Watch starting in 2027, after the state's governor set a target of August 2027 for Apple, Google and Samsung wallets.

item.title: ChatGPT Edu for University of California students from December
item.description: The University of California is paying OpenAI $1.2 million for one year of ChatGPT Edu for all its students, staff and faculty, starting in December. They also get OpenAI's Codex coding agent.
